clue.text: Dim-sighted King in bed

indicators.note: the king sits within the bed, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A ruler lying in bed with failing eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like part of the bedroom scene, but it names Shakespeare's tragic Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleared eyes are blurred and watery, so their owner sees only dimly.

clue.text: Checked — and upbraided

explanation.surface: Someone inspected and then scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Items checked on a list are ticked off; to tick someone off is also to scold them.

clue.text: Record time in completion of partition

indicators.note: the record and the time are set within the word for completion

parts.note: a sum is a total, the completed amount
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record set in the time it takes to finish building a dividing wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The septum is the wall of tissue dividing the nostrils, an anatomical dividing wall.

clue.text: Fighting an opponent of it

parts.note: reads like a battle with a rival, but describes someone who opposes fighting itself

explanation.surface: Someone engaged in combat with their adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rejects war and violence is by definition against combat.

clue.text: Makes up face with oils?

parts.note: suggests applying cosmetic oils to one's face, but means an artist rendering a face in oil paint

explanation.surface: Someone putting on make-up with oily cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist working in oil paint creates a likeness of a sitter's face.

clue.text: Whale said to be worth a considerable amount

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the spelling entered

parts.note: something that could cash a lot is very valuable

explanation.surface: A whale reputed to be extremely valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachalot is another name for the sperm whale.

clue.text: Celebrated mother's return and had a meal out

indicators.note: having a meal out puts the eating around the other piece, so it surrounds

parts.note: fed means ate a meal

indicators.note: the word for mother comes back, read right to left

parts.note: Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A celebration marking mother's homecoming with dinner at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the dinner, but it says the meal word goes around the reversed mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed and celebrated both mean widely known and honoured.

clue.text: Knighted colonel turns to company getting the wind up

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

indicators.note: the colonel's abbreviation is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, such as a colonel

explanation.surface: A knighted officer turns to his firm when a gale blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty Mediterranean wind blowing from North Africa.

clue.text: Girl bitter back in the European capital

indicators.note: the beer word is read backwards

parts.note: bitter is a type of British ale
taken as written

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one, of the word European

explanation.surface: A girl drinking bitter back in a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALE into ELA; 'capital' takes E, the first letter of European. Bitter is a type of British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaine is a female first name, as in the Arthurian lady of Astolat.

clue.text: Where films may be exposed and crimes unheard of

explanation.surface: Photographic film and secret criminal trials side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is exposed inside a photographic device; a case heard in private, away from the public, is held behind closed doors in this Latin phrase.

clue.text: John and I can give up the job

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of the name John
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: John and I are able to quit our work.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack it in is a British idiom for quitting or abandoning something.

clue.text: Kidnap the sailor by the canal

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a duct is a channel or canal, as in the body

explanation.surface: A seaman snatched beside a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, which is kidnapping.

clue.text: Seems mad to order married ladies abroad!

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Ordering seems crazy to wives overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesdames is the French plural of madame, the title for married women in France.

clue.text: Taking trouble to point out

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bothering to make a point clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the taking up of something, such as a child, a policy or an idea.

clue.text: Extension for dining

parts.note: sounds like a building extension for a dining room, but means an extra panel added to the furniture you eat at

explanation.surface: A new room built on for eating meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged or removable board enlarges the top you eat from.

clue.text: A climbing plant in need of air, it was

indicators.note: the letters are in need of repair, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A climbing plant that was gasping for air.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistaria, also spelt wisteria, is a climbing shrub with hanging lilac flowers.

clue.text: The writing is on the wall

definitions.text: The writing is on the wall

parts.words: The writing is on the wall
parts.note: the idiom for impending doom, taken literally as an inscription scrawled on a wall

explanation.surface: The famous warning of approaching disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of scrawled wall inscription, the singular of a familiar plural.

clue.text: Bird that is seen first by raw recruits

parts.note: a rook is a black crow-like bird
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word seen is used

explanation.surface: A bird watched by new soldiers in training.
explanation.definitionFit: Rookies are novices, inexperienced new recruits.

clue.text: Awful cad sure to organise a militant campaign

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess
the letters are organised into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dreadful bounder sets out to lead an aggressive campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause, originally a holy war.

clue.text: Jokes I rarely made about Liberal leader

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
the letters are made into something new
the leading letter of the word Liberal

explanation.surface: I seldom joked about the head of the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges I RARELY; 'about' puts it around L, the first letter of Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or banter.

clue.text: I'm about to stay in the same place

indicators.note: I'm goes round the word for stay

parts.note: taken as written
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: I'm about to remain in the same spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container and 'to stay' the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for the same place, used in footnotes to refer to a source already cited.

clue.text: Where merry men lay down for a kip, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is heard spoken, giving the spelling entered

parts.note: for rest means for a nap; kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's band lie down for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's merry men lived in Sherwood, a woodland setting.

clue.text: Bar in which poets may be found

indicators.note: the letters of poets are found rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub where poets are often discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from a claim.

clue.text: A painter gets out more when the weather's fine

definitions.text: A painter gets out more when the weather's fine

parts.words: A painter gets out more when the weather's fine
parts.note: describes an outdoor artist's habits, pointing to the dry conditions that tempt them outside

explanation.surface: An artist goes outdoors more often in good weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry days without showers are when an outdoor artist can work.

clue.text: The state of this carriage!

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at the poor condition of a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: It names an Australian state and a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: African animals originating from eastern countries

parts.note: lands are countries

explanation.surface: Animals of Africa that came from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes.

clue.text: Has ordered factory-made walking stick

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: Someone has bought a mass-produced cane.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a stick cut from an ash sapling, used for walking.
